book.title: Career and Technical Education Grade 8 Student Textbook
book.subject: cte

title: Four main steps of personal career selection
competency: Discuss the four steps of career selection: research, evaluation, discussion and decision.

keywords.def: Step 1: listing all the career opportunities available in your area.
Step 2: comparing the most suitable careers by resources, knowledge, skills and experience needed.
Step 3: talking with peers to compare selected careers and learn about new ones.
Step 4: choosing one single career based on research, evaluation and discussion.

en.text: Step 1, research: list all careers available in your area: crop production, animal production, manufacturing, construction and services. Step 2, evaluation: compare the most suitable careers on the list, thinking about resources, knowledge level, skills and experience needed. Start from the one you think suits you best.

screens.ask: What should you do first when choosing a career?
opts: List all careers available in your area
Pick the first job you hear about
screens.after: Step 1 is research: list all available career opportunities comprehensively.

screens.title: Step 1: Research
paras: Several career opportunities are available in each locality.
They may be related to animal production, crop production, manufacturing, construction, or services.
Career searching is listing all available career opportunities in the area, comprehensively.

screens.title: Step 2: Evaluate
paras: Compare and contrast the most relevant careers on the list.
Consider: availability of resources, required knowledge level, skills and experience.
Start from the career you think is most appropriate for you, and learn each one in detail.
table: Grade 12 plus nursing diploma or degree

en.text: Step 3, discussion: talk with classmates, compare your chosen careers, explain why you like them, learn about new careers, and sometimes drop a choice. Step 4, decision: choose a single career based on research, evaluation and discussion. Sarkabo's story shows why: doing many businesses at once, he could not manage them and none was profitable, so he chose only poultry.

screens.title: Sarkabo's story
screens.ask: Sarkabo grew barley, teff and coffee, kept 50 chickens and ran a shop, but none made a profit. What did he do?
screens.after: He decided to engage only in poultry production, so he could manage it properly.

screens.title: Step 3: Discuss
paras: Discussion lets you compare the careers you chose and why you liked them.
You may learn about new job tracks from peers.
Two people with the same interest can discuss the requirements further.
You might drop your preferred choice during discussion.

screens.title: Step 4: Decide
paras: Select a single career that seems appropriate, based on research, evaluation and discussion.

Story: Sarkabo finished primary school in 2010 E.C. He farmed barley, teff and coffee, kept 50 chickens and ran a shop. He was not profitable in all of them and could not manage properly. Finally, he chose only poultry production.
